title: Phase 3 study comparing ivonescimab alone or ivonescimab with ligufalimab versus pembrolizumab for the first-line treatment of recurrent and/or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck
official: A randomized, open-label, multicenter, Phase 3 trial of ivonescimab alone or ivonescimab with ligufalimab versus pembrolizumab for the first-line treatment of recurrent and/or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma(HNSCC)
summary: Main objective: To compare the Overall Survival (OS) of ivonescimab in combination with ligufalimab to Standard Of Care (SOC) pembrolizumab and ivonescimab to pembrolizumab in participants with 1 L R/M HNSCC PD-L1 positive (CPS ≥ 1).
conditions: recurrent and/or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck

interventions.name: KEYTRUDA 25 mg/mL concentrate for solution for infusion.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patient capable of voluntary giving her/his written informed consent.
2. Good organ function determined by the following requirements: a.	Haematology (Laboratory test results obtained during the screening period must be satisfactory, and the patient must not have received any blood components or cellgrowth factor support within 14 days prior to the collection of these samples): i.	Absolute neutrophil value (ANC) ≥ 1.5×109/L (1,500/mm3) ii.Platelet count ≥ 100×109/L (100,000/mm3) iii.   Haemoglobin ≥ 10 g/dL b.	Kidneys: i.	Calculated creatinine clearance ≥ 30 mL/min ii.	Urine protein ≤ 2+ or 24 hours (h) urine protein quantification < 1.0 g c.	Liver: i.	Serum total bilirubin ≤ 1.5× upper limit of normal (ULN); for patients with liver metastases or confirmed/suspected Gilbert syndrome, ≤ 3 × ULN ii.	AST and ALT ≤ 2.5×ULN; For patients with liver metastases, AST and ALT ≤ 5×ULN iii.	Serum albumin ≥ 28 g/L d.	Coagulation function: International normalized ratio (INR) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) ≤ 1.5× ULN. This applies only to patients who are not on any anticoagulation. Patients receiving prophylactic-dose anticoagulation could be included and please refer to Exclusion Criterion 24.
3. Patient is willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other requirements of the study as specified in the protocol.
4. Age ≥ 18 and < 80 years old at the time of enrolment
5. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Organization (ECOG) performance status score of 0 or 1.
6. Expected survival ≥ 6 months at randomization.
7. Patient is histologically and/or cytologically confirmed R/M HNSCC that is considered incurable by local therapies (according to the International Union Against Cancer and the American Joint Committee on Cancer 8th edition staging system [Amin et al, 2017]) with a primary tumor initially or currently located in the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx.
8. HPV status test results based on tumor tissue samples must be obtained prior to randomization for patients with oropharyngeal cancer.
9. No prior systemic anti-tumor therapy for R/M HNSCC. Note: Patients who have previously received adjuvant/neoadjuvant chemotherapy with curative intent for non-metastatic disease, radiotherapy, or definitive radiotherapy in combination with chemotherapy or cetuximab/EGFR based therapy for locally advanced disease are eligible if disease progression occurs > 6 months after the end of the last treatment given with curative intent
10. At least one measurable lesion according to RECIST v1.1, or a measurable lesion showing unequivocal radiographic progression after local therapy, and the lesion must be suitable for repeated accurate measurements.
11. Tumors must be PD-L1 positive (CPS ≥ 1). For Europe, PD-L1 positivity is confirmed by local assessment using the PD-L1 IHC 22C3 pharmDx assay (CE-IVD marked in Europe), performed in a laboratory compliant with. applicable national and local certification requirements. For China, PD-L1 positivity must be performed and confirmed by a central laboratory. PD-L1 expression may be evaluated using either archival tumor tissue sample collected prior to the diagnosis of R/M disease, or tumor tissue sample obtained after the diagnosis of R/M disease; a newly obtained biopsy is strongly preferred, though archival tissue is acceptable if a fresh sample cannot be obtained
Exclusion criteria:
1. Primary tumor site (any histology) of nasopharynx, nasal cavity, sinuses, salivary glands, thyroid or parathyroid glands, skin, or unknown primary site of tissue origin.
2. Prior immunotherapy, including any immune checkpoint inhibitors (e.g., anti-PD-1/L1 antibody, anti-CTLA-4 antibody, anti-TIGIT antibody, anti-LAG3 antibody, anti-CD47, anti-SIRPα, etc.), or any immune checkpoint agonists (e.g., ICOS, CD40, CD137, GITR, OX40 antibodies, etc.), immune cell therapy, and any other treatment that targets tumor immunity including therapeutic tumor vaccine, and other adjuvant/neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 based therapy.
3. Patients with ulcers on the skin surface related to the current cancer during the screening period, superficial or protruding skin lesions with excessive surface tension and a greater risk of ulceration, or other patients with a greater risk of ulceration as assessed by the investigator.  Patients with recent tracheostomy involving the tumour which are at risk of bleeding.
4. 8.	Imaging during the screening period shows that the tumor invasion or infiltration of surrounding vital organs (e.g., trachea, oesophagus ) that, in the investigator's assessment, poses a bleeding risk, and/or major blood vessels in the neck (e.g., subclavian artery, common internal, or external carotid artery); patients with other conditions that , in the investigator's judgment, may pose a potential risk of bleeding if they participate in the study; or patients with recent tracheostomy involving the tumor that is associated with a bleeding risk.
5. Presence of brainstem, meningeal metastases, spinal cord metastases or compression, or leptomeningeal disease; or known active brain metastases, uncontrolled by radiotherapy and/or surgery (i.e., symptomatic, new or progressive lesions, or lacking ≥ 4 weeks of stability post-treatment).
6. Received head and neck radiotherapy given with curative intent within 6 months prior to randomization. Palliative radiotherapy treatment for any areas carried out within 3 weeks before randomization; Received non-specific immunomodulatory therapy (such as interleukin, interferon, thymus peptide, tumor necrosis factor, etc.) within 2 weeks prior to randomization, excluding IL-11 for the treatment of thrombocytopenia
7. Presence of active autoimmune disease requiring systemic therapy (e.g., treatment with disease-modifying drugs, corticosteroids, immunosuppressants) within 2 years prior to randomization. Alternative therapies (e.g., thyroxine, insulin, or those targeting the adrenal glands or pituitary) and physiologic corticosteroid replacement therapy for pituitary insufficiency are not considered systemic treatment.
8. Patients with known active tuberculosis and suspected active tuberculosis need to be excluded by clinical examination; Known active syphilis infection.
9. Severe infection within 4 weeks prior to randomization, including but not limited to comorbidities requiring hospitalization, sepsis, or severe pneumonia; Active non-severe infection that has received systemic anti-infective therapy within 2 weeks prior to randomization
10. Patient with malignancies other than HNSCC within 3 years prior to randomization. Patients with other tumors that have been cured through local treatment, such as basal or cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, superficial bladder cancer, cervical or breast carcinoma in situ, are not excluded.
11. Concurrent enrolment in another clinical study, unless it is an observational, non-interventional clinical study or a follow-up period of an interventional study; Received study treatment within 4 weeks prior to randomization.
12. Prior treatment with systemic anti-angiogenic drugs.
13. Previous re-irradiation to the head and neck region.
